heroBody: OLED remains the picture-quality reference for TV in 2026: per-pixel light control, infinite contrast, perfect black levels and wide viewing angles. The Singapore OLED market is dominated by LG Display and Samsung Display panels sold under LG, Samsung, Sony, Panasonic and a handful of value-tier brands, and pricing runs from entry-level 55-inch sets to flagship 77-inch and 83-inch panels at four-figure sums. Singapore's pricing is unusually fragmented because the same panel is sold by authorised distributors (Harvey Norman, Challenger, Courts), marketplace official stores on Shopee and Lazada, Amazon.sg and parallel importers, and the deepest discounts historically land on the 65-inch size where panel volume is highest. This page pulls live Singapore listings from BuyWhere's catalog every few minutes so the price on each card is what Singapore retailers are actually charging right now.

highlightSectionTitle: What changed with OLED TVs in 2026

highlights.title: Brightness has caught up to LED
highlights.body: Early OLEDs were dimmer than premium LED TVs, but the 2026 generation using MLA (Micro Lens Array) on LG panels and QD-OLED on Samsung panels hits peak brightness that matches or beats the best Mini-LED sets. This closes the daylight-viewing gap that used to make OLED a niche pick for dark home theatres; in 2026 you can put an OLED in a bright living room without losing the picture.

highlights.title: The LG C5 vs Samsung S90 question is now a wash
highlights.body: For several cycles LG's C-series OLED was the obvious mainstream pick, with Samsung's QD-OLED models slightly ahead on colour and slightly behind on motion processing. In 2026 the two are essentially indistinguishable on a living-room basis: the C5 still wins on smart-TV polish and gaming features; the Samsung S90 (and its successors) win on colour volume at the cost of a less mature smart-TV platform. The deciding factor for most Singapore buyers is now price and panel size, not panel technology.

highlights.title: 77-inch has become the sweet spot
highlights.body: A 65-inch OLED used to be the sweet spot for price and panel volume. In 2026 the 77-inch size has caught up on price-per-inch and is the new sweet spot for buyers who can fit it — the gap between the 65-inch and 77-inch sticker is much smaller than the diagonal jump suggests, and the panel yields are now mature enough that there is no reliability penalty.

adviceSectionTitle: How to choose an OLED TV in Singapore without overpaying
advicePoints: Pick size first: 55-inch for bedroom or small living room, 65-inch for most Singapore HDB living rooms, 77-inch if you have a 2.5m+ viewing distance and a deep enough console or wall mount.
Check whether the listing is 'local set' or 'Singapore warranty'. Parallel imports are cheaper but the brand's Singapore service centre will not service them under warranty.

Time it: the deepest OLED discounts in Singapore land on the platform sale days (9.9, 10.10, 11.11, 12.12) and during the annual IT Show / PC Show periods; outside those windows the live prices on this page show the current floor.

If you mostly watch Netflix, Disney+ and YouTube, all current OLEDs handle HDR well enough that you do not need to step up to a flagship — the mid-range C-series / S90 deliver the same picture quality for the same content.
For PC use or PS5/Xbox gaming, look for HDMI 2.1 ports on at least two of the inputs and a 120 Hz panel; almost all 2026 OLEDs hit both, but older clearance stock may not.

Buy from a seller with a clear returns policy: OLED burn-in is rare on modern panels but it is not zero, and a 14-day return window protects you from getting a panel with a stuck pixel you only notice after a week.
faqSectionTitle: OLED TVs in Singapore — common questions

faqs.question: Do OLED TVs burn in?
faqs.answer: Modern OLED panels from LG Display and Samsung Display have effective pixel-refresh cycles and screen-shift routines that make burn-in rare for normal TV and movie watching. The risk is mainly for owners who leave a static logo (news channel, stock ticker, HUD on a console) on the screen for many hours a day, every day. If your viewing is mostly varied TV and film, burn-in is not a practical concern.

faqs.question: LG OLED vs Samsung OLED in Singapore — which is better?
faqs.answer: For most Singapore buyers, they are a wash. LG's C-series still has the more mature smart platform (webOS) and slightly better gaming features; Samsung's QD-OLED panels win on colour volume at the cost of a less mature smart platform. If you already use an Apple TV or a PlayStation 5 as your main source, the smart platform is irrelevant and you should pick on price and size.

faqs.question: When is an OLED TV cheapest in Singapore?
faqs.answer: Historically during platform sale days (9.9, 10.10, 11.11, 12.12) on Shopee and Lazada, and during the IT Show / PC Show periods at Harvey Norman and Challenger. Outside those windows, the live listings on this page show the current floor.

faqs.question: Is 77-inch too big for a Singapore HDB living room?
faqs.answer: A 77-inch TV fits a typical 4-room HDB living room at a viewing distance of about 2.5m. The rule of thumb is the TV should be roughly half the viewing distance in inches for an immersive cinema feel, and a third the distance for a comfortable everyday TV feel — at 2.5m viewing distance, 77-inch sits at the immersive end of comfortable.

categoryIntro.heading: Why Singapore OLED TV prices move with platform sales
categoryIntro.body: Singapore OLED pricing is shaped by the platform sale calendar more than by the TV brands. The same LG C5 sold by Harvey Norman, an Amazon.sg third-party seller, a Shopee Mall official store and a Carousell parallel importer will land at four different prices, and the gap between the highest and lowest can be a meaningful chunk of the panel's value. Prices move most on Shopee and Lazada's quarterly sale days (9.9, 10.10, 11.11, 12.12) and during the IT Show / PC Show physical expos, with Amazon.sg usually matching a day or two later. That is why a static 'best OLED TV in Singapore' article goes stale within weeks and why this page reads live listings instead.
